jobs.title: Analyst - Corporate Risk Solutions
jobs.description:
Do you want your voice heard and your actions to count?

Discover your opportunity with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), one of the world’s leading financial groups. Across the globe, we’re 150,000 colleagues, striving to make a difference for every client, organization, and community we serve. We stand for our values, building long-term relationships, serving society, and fostering shared and sustainable growth for a better world.

With a vision to be the world’s most trusted financial group, it’s part of our culture to put people first, listen to new and diverse ideas and collaborate toward greater innovation, speed and agility. This means investing in talent, technologies, and tools that empower you to own your career.

Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.

The selected colleague will work at an MUFG office or client sites four days per week and work remotely one day. A member of our recruitment team will provide more details.

Analyst – Corporate Risk Solutions

Overview of the Department

As an Analyst within the Corporate Risk Solutions Group, you’ll support our North American corporate

clients in managing the interest rate and currency risks associated with their financing and broader

business activities through derivatives.

Our product offering includes interest rate swaps, cross-currency swaps, foreign exchange derivatives,

and interest rate options.

Main Purpose of the Role

Support the Corporate Risk Solutions sales team in delivering a high-quality client experience and

achieving the desk’s objectives, with primary responsibility for accurate and timely trade booking,

execution support, post-trade coordination, and maintenance of robust operational controls.

Key Responsibilities

Book derivative transactions accurately and promptly in relevant systems, verifying economics

against confirmations, trader recaps, and client instructions and resolving discrepancies before

downstream processing

Provide day-to-day execution and post-trade support, including trade capture, lifecycle-event

coordination, settlement follow-up, documentation tracking, and investigation of booking or

operational breaks

Coordinate with salespeople, traders, operations, legal, compliance, and other internal partners

to ensure transactions progress efficiently from pricing and execution through confirmation and

settlement

Support pricing requests and trade executions by gathering complete transaction details,

preparing internal records, and communicating accurate information to relevant stakeholders

Bachelor’s degree required

Strong attention to detail and a consistent focus on accuracy and operational controls
Ability to manage multiple time-sensitive tasks, prioritize effectively, and take ownership of

items through completion

Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across sales,

trading, operations, and control functions

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify, investigate, and

resolve trade or booking discrepancies

Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint highly preferred
Experience with Bloomberg beneficial
Fluency in English required

The typical base pay range for this role is between $110K - $115K depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience and location. This role may also be eligible for certain discretionary performance-based bonus and/or incentive compensation. Additionally, our Total Rewards program provides colleagues with a competitive benefits package (in accordance with the eligibility requirements and respective terms of each) that includes comprehensive health and wellness benefits, retirement plans, educational assistance and training programs, income replacement for qualified employees with disabilities, paid maternity and parental bonding leave, and paid vacation, sick days, and holidays. For more information on our Total Rewards package, please click the link below.

We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws (including (i) the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, (ii) the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, (iii) the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, and (iv) the California Fair Chance Act) to the extent that (a) an applicant is not subject to a statutory disqualification pursuant to Section 3(a)(39) of the Securities and Exchange Act of 1934 or Section 8a(2) or 8a(3) of the Commodity Exchange Act, and (b) they do not conflict with the background screening requirements of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) and the National Futures Association (NFA). The major responsibilities listed above are the material job duties of this role for which the Company reasonably believes that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship potentially resulting in the withdrawal of conditional offer of employment, if any.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities duties and skills required of personnel so classified.

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and committed to leveraging the diverse backgrounds, perspectives and experience of our workforce to create opportunities for our colleagues and our business. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, religion, gender expression, gender identity, sex, age, ancestry, marital status, protected veteran and military status, disability, medical condition, sexual orientation, genetic information, or any other status of an individual or that individual’s associates or relatives that is protected under applicable federal, state, or local law.

jobs.title: Data & Epidemiology Analytics Director
jobs.description:
Role:
The Director of Real-World Data & Epidemiology (RWD & Epi) Analytics leads the design, execution, and communication of observational studies using diverse real-world data sources.

Responsibilities:
Collaborate with asset leaders to develop study protocols, perform feasibility assessments, conduct survival and economic modeling, manage data analysis, and interpret results for technical and non-technical audiences. Lead pilots for AI applications, evaluate new data modalities, mentor scientists, and define standardized processes for study execution and data management. Contribute to infrastructure development, ensure compliance, and support strategic objectives within the department.

Qualifications & Skills:
Requires a graduate degree (PhD or Master's) in Epidemiology, Biostatistics, or related fields with 10+ years of experience in RWE and epidemiology analytics. Expertise in observational study design, advanced statistical methods, and proficiency in programming languages (SAS, R, Python). Strong communication, stakeholder management, and leadership skills are essential, with oncology experience preferred.

Key Duties:
Manage study lifecycle from feasibility to reporting, evaluate emerging data modalities, lead AI initiatives, mentor team members, and contribute to analytics infrastructure. Work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment, applying strategic and scientific expertise to inform clinical and market decisions.

jobs.title: Systems Analyst
jobs.description:
Marketing Statement

NYC Health + Hospitals is the largest public health care system in the United States. We provide essential outpatient, inpatient and home-based services to more than one million New Yorkers every year across the city’s five boroughs. Our large health system consists of ambulatory centers, acute care centers, post-acute care/long-term care, rehabilitation programs, Home Care, and Correctional Health Services. Our diverse workforce is uniquely focused on empowering New Yorkers.

At NYC Health + Hospitals, our mission is to deliver high quality care health services, without exception. Every employee takes a person-centered approach that exemplifies the ICARE values (Integrity, Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence) through empathic communication and partnerships between all persons.

Duties & Responsibilities

Purpose of Position
:

Under supervision, implements newly designed systems and parallel systems; revises existing systems, methods, procedures and designs. Performs analysis and modifies systems, procedures and forms to effect improvements, increase effectiveness in process flows and optimization of Corporate productivity.

Examples Of Typical Tasks

Studies, reviews and analyzes existing systems, methods, procedures and projects to determine whether systems meet the operational needs of the Corporation.
Prepares and modifies flow charts, diagrams, reports and other documentation necessary for systems design and modification.
Participates in the training of staff in the implementation of new programs and systems design.
Prepares manuals of systems and procedures, reviews and modifies existing manuals.
Recommends improvements and/or modifications of existing systems in terms of problems, bottlenecks and inadequate utilization of resources.
Implements the development of approval systems and subsystems.
Designs and implements approval parallel systems to minimize operational problems.
Maintains, modifies, improves and monitors existing operational systems, standards of performance, quality of controls and progress of assigned projects with a view towards computer applications.
Utilizes industrial engineering techniques and/or administrative management techniques to establish performance standards and input data, and analyzes alternative means of deriving input data and recommends the optimal method.

Minimum Qualifications

A Baccalaureate Degree in a relevant field from an accredited college or university; and,
One year of experience in business, government, hospital, educational institute or non-profit organization in analysis, development and implementation of systems, methods and procedures, management information development and data coordination. Familiarity with EDP applications and data processing programs; or,
A Masters Degree in Management, Business Administration, Hospital Administration Management, Public Administration, Accounting or relevant field from an accredited college or university; or,
A satisfactory combination of education, training and experience.

Department Preferences

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities And Other Requirements

Contact Center Operations and Quality Auditing
Quality Evaluation Processes and Software
Ambulatory Care Front Desk Operations and Scheduling
Self-starter and ability to work independently.
Strong organizational skills, meets deadlines and carries out duties efficiently.
Successfully prioritizes competing tasks
Ability to analyze and identify agent trending
Effective communication (written and oral).
Ability to overcome organizational resistance to change.
Experience with creating or compiling reports using various sources of data.
Strong Leadership Skills
Must be extremely detail oriented with the ability to collaborate with Operations to create thorough corrective and preventative plans.
1-3 Years Healthcare or Contact Center Quality background preferred.
1-3 Years Contact Center experience preferred
Calabrio (or similar Quality Evaluation Software)
Epic
MS Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)

How To Apply

If you wish to apply for this position, please apply online by clicking the "Apply for Job" button.

jobs.title: Data & Systems Reporting Analyst
jobs.description:
About Empower Community Care

Empower Community Care is a family of mission-driven organizations delivering evidence-based behavioral health, child welfare, and community care programs and services. Our portfolio includes BSFT, Carey Group, Evidence-Based Associates (EBA), FFT LLC, MST Services, Orbis, and The Incredible Years — each advancing outcomes for children, families, and the communities we serve.

Position Summary

The Data & Systems Reporting Analyst builds and maintains data systems, runs recurring and ad hoc reports, and verifies data for accuracy, completeness, and usability across EBA projects. The role focuses on creating reliable, user-friendly data tools and high-quality information that support implementation, decision-making, continuous quality improvement, and external reporting- to strengthen services to children and families, providers, and public partners. Project examples may include statewide implementation initiatives, evidence-based practice reporting, provider performance monitoring, recruitment tracking, and funder reporting.

Key Responsibilities

Data Systems Development & Integration

Build, configure, and maintain databases, systems, workflows, automations, and surveys (including survey logic, embedded data, and dashboard configurations) that support EBA project operations, reduce duplication, and ensure consistent data entry
Translate program, funder, and implementation requirements into practical data structures, validation rules, and user-friendly reporting tools
Support data integration and reconciliation across numerous platforms
Clean, normalize, and prepare client, provider, fidelity, outcome, capacity, implementation, and fiscal data for analysis, reporting, and quality review

Reporting & Analytics

Run recurring (monthly, quarterly, annual) and ad hoc reports and dashboards: including data pulls, validation, analysis, and formatting — spanning scorecards, executive summaries, activity/capacity/fidelity/outcome reports, and implementation-monitoring tools
Prepare project-specific reporting packages and funder/stakeholder deliverables, such as Monthly Activity Reports, statewide data submissions, and performance scorecards
Maintain registries or tracking tools for participants, providers, therapists, competencies, training milestones, and fidelity indicators
Review report outputs for accuracy, clarity, and usefulness before sharing with project teams, leadership, funders, providers, or external partners

Data Quality & Performance Monitoring

Verify and monitor data accuracy, completeness, consistency, and integrity — across client, provider, fidelity, performance, implementation, and fiscal data — through routine audits and validation reviews
Investigate discrepancies, missing or duplicate records, workflow gaps, and system defects across source systems; maintain data quality controls, audit trails, and remediation processes
Conduct testing (user acceptance, dashboard, survey, and workflow) and recommend improvements to data collection, reporting, and monitoring based on QA findings and stakeholder feedback

Documentation & Training Support

Create and maintain data dictionaries, reporting specifications, SOPs, workflow documentation, user guides, and training materials
Collaborate with project teams, trainers, providers, and external partners to ensure data systems are practical, accurate, and aligned with implementation, reporting, fidelity monitoring, and continuous improvement needs
Prepare and present reports, dashboards, findings, and insights that are accurate, accessible, and useful for leadership, project teams, funders, state partners, providers, and trainers

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in data analytics, statistics, computer science, information systems, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered
2–4 years of experience building, maintaining, or improving data systems, reports, and dashboards — including data cleaning, validation, integration, analysis, and quality assurance — for internal and external stakeholders
Working knowledge and experience in common data, reporting, or database tools; direct experience with specific platforms may be gained on the job
Ability to manage recurring reporting cycles, project-based timelines, and competing priorities
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences
Ability to work remotely and independently, with availability during core business hours in Eastern Time (ET); ability to pass a required background check and comply with the confidentiality and data-privacy requirements described under Additional Requirements below

Preferred Skills & Experience

Data systems: QuickBase or other low-code/no-code platforms, relational tables, formulas, forms, reports, dashboards, and workflow automation
Survey and data collection: Qualtrics survey design, display/skip logic, embedded data, workflows, dashboards, APIs, automations, and data exports
CRM and engagement tracking: HubSpot, Salesforce, or similar systems used for contact, provider, county, or stakeholder tracking
Reporting and visualization: Power BI, Excel, scorecards, dashboards, and stakeholder-ready summaries
Field experience: Familiarity with behavioral health, child and family services, juvenile justice, child welfare, evidence-based practices, public-sector reporting, or nonprofit program evaluation

Additional Requirements

Background Check: Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check, consistent with applicable law and the sensitivity of the data handled in this role
Confidentiality & Data Privacy: This role involves regular access to client, provider, fidelity, and fiscal data across behavioral health, child welfare, and juvenile justice programs. The employee must maintain strict confidentiality and comply with all applicable data-privacy requirements, including HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 where applicable, as well as Empower's internal data governance policies
Work Environment: This is a remote, computer-based position requiring prolonged periods of sitting and extended use of a computer, keyboard, and video conferencing tools. Reasonable accommodations will be made for qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with the ADA
Other Duties: This job description reflects the general nature and level of work performed and is not intended to be a comprehensive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice

Benefits

Empower Community Care offers a competitive total-rewards package, which includes medical, dental, and vision coverage; retirement savings; paid time off and holidays; and life insurance.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Empower Community Care is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.
